Relative to a neutral macro communiqué, the September 2023 FOMC statement is a hawkish hold: the target range is maintained at 5.25–5.50%, balance-sheet runoff continues, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks despite low unemployment and “solid” recent growth.

Incorporating the latest Beige Book softens that read. Most Districts reported slight-to-modest overall growth, mixed consumer spending, continued but easing labor tightness with moderating wage pressures, and slower—but still elevated—price increases. Credit conditions tightened further, loan demand weakened across households and businesses, and commercial real estate—especially office—deteriorated. These developments corroborate the statement’s warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring and temper the “solid” growth characterization.

Netting the restrictive policy stance and persistent inflation concerns against Beige Book evidence of moderating demand, easing wage/price trends, and tighter credit, the assessment shifts closer to neutral and more risk-managed than a pure read of the statement. Adjusting for the Beige Book, the tone moves from modestly hawkish toward balanced/cautious.
